text:
Andrew Brunette said it after Minnesota beat his Predators 7-3 on Tuesday, per NHL.com's Heather Rule: "They might be the best line in the NHL." He meant Kirill Kaprizov, Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy, and the numbers agree with him. In 242 minutes together at five on five they have outscored opponents 20-1, with 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Twenty to one is not sustainable. The chances underneath it are still elite.

The Wild are 16-3-4, have won four straight and have points in 12 consecutive games, per Rule. Unlike some hot teams, the process backs it: they get 56% of the expected goals, which is what good teams look like, and the forwards are scoring about what they should. Where they've gotten help is the net. They've allowed more than 15 fewer goals than their chances against suggest, and Jesper Wallstedt is 5-0-0 with a .936 save percentage over his last five starts.

The roster got stronger this week, too. Brock Faber made his season debut after a skull fracture and, per NHL.com, didn't miss a beat. Quinn Hughes anchors both top pairs. John Hynes's team is 99% to make the playoffs by our odds. The one thing to watch is the goaltending regressing toward normal, because the rest of this team looks real.
